additions.text: The chocolate shop
chocolate maker
It is a chocolate shop. It smells very good. There is white, dark and milk chocolate. Greta works here.
Hi, I am Greta. Do you like chocolate?
Greta lets you taste three chocolates. Which one do you want?
The white chocolate, please.
Greta says: “It is very sweet. Children love it!”
The dark chocolate.
Greta says: “It is my favourite. It is a little bitter.”
The milk chocolate.
Greta says: “It is the most popular. How many do you want?”
Greta asks: “Is it a present?” She puts the chocolate in a red box. Who is it for?
Do you like chocolate?
Yes, I like it a lot. / Not much.
White, dark or milk?
When do you eat chocolate?
Do you like sweet things?
Yes, I like them. / I prefer salty things.
What is your favourite dessert?
Do you make desserts?
Who do you buy presents for?
For my mother / my partner / my friends.
What do you give them?
Do you like getting presents?
Is it cold in your city?
Yes, it is very cold. / No, it is hot.
What do you drink when it is cold?
Do you like the cold?
chocolate
sweet
bitter
the present
the box

Mitre Street, in the centre of Bariloche, has many chocolate shops. Greta comes from a family that arrived from Switzerland many years ago. In the window there is “chocolate en rama”, bonbons and alfajores.
My grandfather started with a small kitchen at home. Now the shop has three floors. Upstairs we make the chocolate and downstairs we sell it. Do you want to see how we make it?
You have money for one thing only. What do you buy?
A big box of “chocolate en rama”.
Greta explains it breaks easily and gives you a special bag for the trip.
Six alfajores to share.
Greta adds one more as a gift. “Always one more for the road.”
A one-hour class in the kitchen.
You put on an apron and make your own bonbons. They are not perfect, but they are yours.
The power goes out in the whole street. The chocolate in the kitchen starts to harden. Greta asks for your help. What do you do?
What typical food is there in your city?
In my city there is… / It is famous for…
Do you like it?
Where do you buy it?
Does your family come from another country?
Yes, my grandparents come from… / No, they are all from here.
What customs do they have?
Do you speak another language at home?
Can you cook something sweet?
Yes, I can make… / No, I can only eat.
Who taught you?
Who do you cook for?
What do you buy as a souvenir of a trip?
I always buy… / I don’t buy anything.
What is your favourite souvenir?
Where do you keep it?
the shop window
the bonbon
the apron
the souvenir
to share

It is high season and the chocolate shop is full of tourists and school groups on their graduation trip. Greta has been working since seven in the morning. A boy from one of the groups breaks a two-kilo chocolate figure.

Every year it is the same: thousands of fifteen- and sixteen-year-olds arrive, happy and without sleep. I love them, really, but that figure was a Saint Bernard that took me three days to make. Did you go on a trip like that with your school?
The boy is very nervous and has no money. The group coordinator is nowhere to be found. What do you advise Greta?
Call the travel company so they pay.
The company pays, but it takes two months. Greta sighs and keeps the invoice.
Have the boy help in the shop for an afternoon.
The boy works four hours, learns to make bonbons and in the end wants to come back next year.
Use the pieces to sell broken chocolate cheaper.
The tourists buy all the pieces in half an hour. Greta earns more than with the whole figure.
That night, the whole group comes back to the shop with a sign: “Sorry, Greta.” Each of them buys something.
Did you go on a school trip?
Yes, we went to… / No, we never went on a trip.
What do you remember from that trip?
Did you do anything forbidden?
Have you ever broken something expensive?
Yes, once I broke… / No, I am very careful.
What happened afterwards?
Did you have to pay?
What place in your country fills up with tourists?
In summer / winter, … fills up with…
Is it good for the people there?
Do you go in high season?
Have you ever worked with the public?
Yes, I worked in… / No, never.
Who was the most difficult customer?
Did you like it?
high season
graduation trip
to break
the invoice
the piece

An international chain wants to buy Greta’s family chocolate shop. It offers a lot of money and promises to keep the name, but wants to change the recipe for a cheaper one and move production to a factory in Buenos Aires.

My brother wants to sell. He says we are tired, that the business gets harder every year and that with that money we could live in peace. He is right about everything. But if they change the recipe, it is no longer our chocolate, it is just our surname on a box. What would you do?
Greta has to give an answer on Monday. What do you recommend?
Sell, but on condition that they keep the recipe.
The chain accepts it in the contract, but only for five years. After that, nobody knows.
Don’t sell and look for a smaller local partner.
A local hotel partners with them. They earn less, but the kitchen stays above the shop.
Sell everything and open something new and small under her own name.
Greta opens a ten-metre workshop. The queue of customers reaches the corner.
In an old box, Greta finds her grandfather’s recipe notebook. The original recipe is not the one they use today: it was already changed thirty years ago, without anyone noticing.
Would you sell a family business for a lot of money?
Yes, if… / No, because…
What condition would you set?
What would your family think?
What product from your country has lost quality over the years?
Before, … was better, now…
Why do you think it happened?
Do you still buy it?
Is it important that a tradition never changes?
I think so / not, because…
Can you give an example?
What tradition would you change?
Do you prefer small shops or big chains?
I prefer… because…
Where did you last buy something?
Would you pay more for local products?
the chain (of shops)
the business partner
the recipe
the surname
to notice
The lake harbour
boat captain
It is a big blue lake. There are mountains with snow. There is a white boat. Don Aníbal is the captain.
Good morning. I am Aníbal. Are you coming on the boat?
The boat goes to an island. Where do you sit?
Outside, to see the lake.
Aníbal says: “It is cold. Put on a jacket!”
Inside, near the window.
Aníbal says: “Good idea. There is hot coffee.”
With the captain, please.
Aníbal says: “Sure! Come. Here is the wheel.”
There are birds around the boat. Aníbal gives you bread. “Feed them!” What do you do?
Do you like boats?
Yes, I like them. / No, I get seasick.
Are there boats in your city?
Can you swim?
Is there a lake near your home?
Yes, there is a lake. / No, there is a river / the sea.
What is it called?
Do you go often?
What colour are the mountains in winter?
They are white. / They are green.
Do you like snow?
Is there snow in your country?
Do you like birds?
Yes, a lot. / Not much.
Do you have pets?
What is your favourite animal?
the lake
the boat
the island
snow
the jacket (Argentina)

Lake Nahuel Huapi is huge and the water is very cold, even in summer. From the harbour, boats leave for Victoria Island and the arrayán forest, trees with cinnamon-coloured trunks. Don Aníbal has been driving boats here for forty years.
This lake changes its mood like a person. In the morning it is calm, in the afternoon there is wind and waves. Today the day is perfect. Is it your first time in Patagonia?
There are three excursions today. Which do you choose?
The arrayán forest.
You walk along a wooden path among orange trees. It looks like a fairy tale.
Victoria Island, with a long walk.
You walk for three hours. You see ancient paintings on the rocks and a white-sand beach.
A short trip round the lake and back.
Aníbal tells you stories about the lake and shows you where a very rare bird lives.
Suddenly the wind starts and the boat rocks a lot. A woman gets scared. What do you do?
Do you prefer the mountains or the beach?
Where do you go on holiday?
What do you do there?
Do you swim in cold water?
Yes, I love it. / No, never!
Where do you swim?
How long can you stay in?
What do you like doing when it is sunny?
When it is sunny, I like…
And when it rains?
With whom?
Does anything scare you when travelling?
Planes / boats… scare me. / Nothing.
What do you do to stay calm?
Has it always been like that?
the harbour
the wave
the wind
the path
the forest

It is the last trip of the day and night is falling. Don Aníbal tells the legend of Nahuelito, a huge creature that, according to some locals, lives at the bottom of the lake. Many people laugh, but there are blurry photos from the eighties.

I didn’t believe in Nahuelito. One winter afternoon, in ’92, I saw a long shadow beside the boat, bigger than the boat itself. I told my wife and she laughed for three days straight. Do you believe in these things?
A passenger says he sees something moving in the water. Everyone looks. What do you do?
I take a photo quickly.
The photo comes out blurry, like all of them. Now you too have your Nahuelito photo.
I ask Aníbal to stop the boat.
Aníbal turns off the engine. Total silence. Only the water can be heard. Nobody breathes.
I laugh: it is surely a log.
Aníbal smiles: “That is exactly what I said in ’92.”
When they reach the harbour, a little boy asks Aníbal if Nahuelito is bad. Aníbal answers: “No. He is shy, like you.”
Is there a legend in your country?
Yes, they say that… / I don’t know any.
Who told it to you?
Do people believe it?
Have you ever seen something strange?
Yes, once I saw… / No, never.
Where were you?
Did you tell anyone?
What stories did people tell you as a child?
My grandmother / my father used to tell me…
Did they scare you?
Do you tell them now?
Do you like watching the sunset?
Yes, especially in… / I don’t pay attention to it.
What is the most beautiful sunset you have seen?
Who were you with?
the legend
the shadow
blurry
to get dark
the little boy (Argentina)

An investment group wants to build a private pier and a luxury hotel on a bay of the lake that is public today. There would be work for a hundred people, but locals could no longer swim or fish there. Don Aníbal has to speak at the neighbourhood meeting tonight.

My grandson needs work and that hotel would give him a job. But my father taught me to swim in that bay, and his father taught him. If we close it, today’s kids will only see the lake from the road. I don’t know what to say tonight. What would you say?
Aníbal has five minutes to speak. What do you suggest?
Support the hotel, but demand that the beach stays public.
The investors accept a twenty-metre public strip. Some locals call him a traitor; others, sensible.
Oppose it and propose the hotel somewhere else.
The meeting lasts four hours. In the end, the town council asks for a study of other sites.
Tell his personal story and not say how to vote.
The room goes quiet. Several young people change their minds, and some old ones too.
After the meeting, Aníbal’s grandson confesses that he already signed a contract with the hotel last week.
Should natural places always be public?
Are there exceptions?
What happens in your country?
What is more important: jobs or the landscape?
It depends on… / For me, …
Can you have both?
What example do you know?
Have you ever taken part in a neighbourhood meeting?
Yes, once we discussed… / No, I never went.
How did it end?
Did you speak?
What place from your childhood has changed a lot?
Before it was… and now it is…
For better or worse?
Do you go back sometimes?
the pier
the bay
to demand
the town council
sensible
Cerro Catedral
ski instructor
It is a mountain with a lot of snow. There are people with skis. It is very cold. Lola is the ski teacher.
Hi! I am Lola. Can you ski?
Lola has three activities. What do you want to do?
I want to ski.
Lola says: “Very good! Slowly at first.”
I want to go up on the chairlift.
Lola says: “Up there, there is a very nice view.”
I want to drink a hot chocolate.
Lola says: “Me too! Let’s go to the café.”
You fall in the snow! Lola laughs and gives you her hand. What do you say?
Do you like winter?
Yes, I like it. / No, I prefer summer.
Why?
What do you do in winter?
Do you do any sport?
Yes, I play… / No, I don’t do sport.
When?
What clothes do you wear when it is cold?
I wear a jacket / hat / gloves.
Do you have a scarf?
What colour is it?
Do you like mountains?
Yes, a lot. / I prefer the sea.
Are there mountains in your country?
Which is the highest?
the mountain
to ski
the chairlift
the cold
to fall

Cerro Catedral is one of the largest ski resorts in South America. In July, families arrive from all over the country and from Brazil. Lola teaches beginners from nine in the morning until four in the afternoon.
My students today are a family from São Paulo. They had never seen snow. The kids are happy and the parents are scared to death. Will you help me translate a little?
The dad doesn’t want to go down the slope. What do you tell him?
“Relax, we go very slowly.”
The dad takes fifteen minutes to go down a hundred-metre slope. At the end, he claps.
“Look at your kids: they can do it!”
The dad looks at the kids, breathes and goes down. He falls twice, but laughs.
“You can wait in the café.”
The dad happily accepts. From the window, he takes photos of the whole family.
The youngest girl of the family gets lost in the crowd. Lola asks you to look for her in the café. What do you do?
Have you ever seen snow?
Yes, in… / No, never.
What did you do?
What sport do you want to learn?
I want to learn to…
Is it expensive?
What languages do you speak?
I speak… and a little…
Where do you use them?
Which is the hardest?
Did you ever get lost as a child?
Yes, once in… / No, never.
Who found you?
Were you scared?
the slope
the beginner
slowly
the little girl (Argentina)
to get lost
This winter it hardly snowed. The lower slopes are green and only the upper ones are open. Hotels are lowering their prices and many instructors, like Lola, are working half the hours.

When I was a girl, in July the snow reached our front door. Now we check the forecast every morning as if it were the lottery. Last year I thought about going to work in Europe, in the Alps, but there is not enough snow there either. Have you noticed changes in the climate where you live?
Lola has few classes this month. What do you advise her?
Offer mountain walks without snow.
Lola organises sunrise walks. Tourists who don’t ski are delighted.
Go to the northern hemisphere in December.
Lola gets work in Canada for their winter. Two winters a year: lots of cold and few holidays.
Give online ski lessons, with videos.
Her “how not to fall” videos get thousands of views. Now people recognise her on the slope.
That night it starts snowing hard and doesn’t stop for three days. Lola’s phone won’t stop ringing.
What was the weather like when you were a child?
Before it was more… / It was the same.
What has changed?
Does it worry you?
Does your work depend on the weather?
Yes, when it rains… / No, not at all.
What do you do on a bad day?
Do you know someone whose does?
Would you work in another country for a season?
Yes, in… / No, because…
What job would you do?
What would you miss?
What did you use to do in the winter holidays?
We used to go to… / I stayed at home and…
Do you still do it?
to snow
the forecast
the sunrise
the season
to miss

The ski resort wants to make artificial snow to secure the season. For that it needs to take millions of litres of water from a mountain stream. Park rangers and some Mapuche communities in the area oppose it. Lola works for the resort, but she is also a volunteer in an environmental group.

My boss asked me to appear in the promotional video for the artificial snow. My friends in the environmental group asked me to sign a letter against it. If I say yes to the video, I lose my friends; if I sign the letter, I might lose my job. How do you get out of this?
Lola has to answer both before Friday. What do you recommend?
Sign the letter and explain to her boss why.
Her boss doesn’t fire her, but gives her the earliest shifts of the whole season.
Do neither.
Nobody is happy. Both sides tell her that having no opinion is also an opinion.
Propose a meeting between the resort and the communities.
The meeting takes place. There is no agreement yet, but for the first time they sit at the same table.
A journalist reports that the resort had already started taking water from the stream before getting the permit. Lola appears in the background of the article’s photo, without knowing it.
Have you had to choose between your job and your beliefs?
Yes, once… / It has never happened to me, but…
What did you choose?
Would you do the same today?
Does tourism help or harm nature?
On the one hand… on the other hand…
What kind of tourism do you prefer?
Who should decide about a region’s water?
I think … should decide.
And if they don’t agree?
What is it like in your country?
Is it possible to be neutral in a conflict like this?
Have you ever been caught in the middle?
How did you feel?
artificial snow
the stream
the park ranger
to fire (from a job)
the permit
The brewery
brewer
It is a wooden bar. There are long tables and many people. Bruno makes the beer here. There is food too.
Hi! I am Bruno. What would you like to drink?
Bruno has three drinks. What do you order?
A blonde beer, please.
Bruno says: “It is light and fresh. Cheers!”
A dark beer.
Bruno says: “It tastes of coffee and chocolate.”
A lemonade, please.
Bruno says: “Sure! It is homemade, with mint.”
Bruno brings a big pizza. “It is for sharing.” There are eight slices. How many do you eat?
What do you drink with food?
I drink water / juice / wine.
And at a party?
What don’t you like?
Do you like pizza?
What do you like on it?
How many slices do you eat?
Do you go to bars with friends?
Yes, on Fridays. / No, I prefer home.
What is your favourite bar?
What do you order?
What food do you share?
I share pizza / chips…
Do you like sharing?
beer
the bar
the slice
homemade
Cheers!
Bariloche has many craft breweries. Bruno makes his beer with mountain water and hops from El Bolsón, a nearby town. At night the place fills up with tired skiers and musicians who play for free.
This beer is called “Nahuelito”. I made it last year and it won a prize. But my favourite is the raspberry one, although hardly anyone orders it. Do you want to try both?
Bruno wants a name for his new beer. What do you suggest?
“Catedral”, like the mountain.
Bruno says there is already one with that name. “Bariloche is small, we all copy!”
“Lola”, after the ski instructor.
Bruno blushes. It seems he likes Lola a lot.
A name in Mapuche.
Bruno decides to ask a teacher from the school to choose the word properly.
The beer fridge breaks. Bruno has forty litres of warm beer and a party in two hours. What do you do?
What typical drink is there in your country?
In my country people drink…
When do people drink it?
What do people do in your city at night?
They go out to… / They stay at home.
And you?
Until what time?
Do you play an instrument?
Yes, I play the… / No, but I would like to.
Since when?
What music do you like?
What name would you give a bar?
I would call it “…” because…
What would the place be like?
What music would there be?
craft / handmade
the prize
raspberry
the fridge (Argentina)
to try / taste

It is Saturday and there is a mountain-cooking contest at the brewery. Each participant prepares a dish with trout, lamb or local mushrooms. Bruno is on the jury, but one of the cooks is his ex-girlfriend.

Look, I’m not going to lie: Carla’s dish is the best. But if I give her the prize, the whole town will say I am still in love. And if I don’t, she will say I hold a grudge. Something similar happened to me two years ago. What would you do?
Bruno has to vote now. What do you tell him?
Vote for the best dish, without thinking about anything else.
Carla wins. Some people whisper, but the lamb really was incredible.
Not vote and explain why.
The audience applauds his honesty. The other two judges choose Carla anyway.
Vote for the second best.
Carla comes second by one point. That night, Bruno can’t sleep.
After the contest, Carla goes up to Bruno and suggests opening a restaurant together, next to the brewery.
Have you ever taken part in a contest?
Yes, a … contest and I won. / Yes, but I didn’t win. / No, never.
Were you nervous?
What did you learn?
Are you friends with an ex?
Yes, we get on well. / No, we prefer not to talk.
Is it possible to be friends?
What do your friends think?
What is the tastiest dish you have tried?
Once I tried… in…
Who cooked it?
Can you make it?
Is it easy to be fair with people you know?
Has it ever happened to you?
the contest
the jury
trout
lamb
resentful / holding a grudge

A big drinks company has bought several craft breweries in Patagonia. Now it is offering Bruno nationwide distribution in every supermarket. It would be a huge success, but he would have to produce ten times more and stop selling only in his bar.

When I started, twelve years ago, I made beer in my mother’s kitchen, in soup pots. My friends told me I was crazy. Now they are offering me what I always dreamed of, and yet I am afraid of becoming just another factory. Craft is not only the recipe: it is the time, the people, this place. Do you think you can grow without losing that?
Bruno has to sign or reject the deal. What do you advise him?
Accept, but with one beer only, and keep the others in the bar.
“Nahuelito” reaches the whole country. The others remain a local secret.
Reject it and grow slowly, with other brewers in the area.
Five breweries set up a cooperative. They earn less, but they decide together.
Accept everything and seize the opportunity.
In one year Bruno earns more than in ten. But he is hardly ever at the bar now and the musicians stop coming.
Bruno discovers that the company has also secretly bought the hop farm in El Bolsón that sells to him and to every brewer in the area.
Can you grow a lot without losing your identity?
Yes, if… / It is hard because…
Do you know an example?
And in people?
What dream did you have when you were young that you haven’t fulfilled yet?
I always wanted to… but…
Is it still possible?
What are you missing?
What do you think of cooperatives?
I think they are… because…
Is there one in your city?
Would you work in one?
Has anyone told you you were crazy because of a project?
Yes, when I wanted to… / No, never.
Were they right?
What would you tell them today?
to distribute
the pot
hops
the cooperative
to take advantage of
The Centro Cívico
tour guide
It is a big square with stone and wooden buildings. There is a tower with a clock. There are big white dogs. Inés is a guide.
Hi, I am Inés. Welcome to Bariloche! Where are you from?
There is a Saint Bernard dog. You can take a photo with the dog. What do you do?
I take a photo with the dog.
Inés says: “What a nice photo! The dog is called Rocco.”
I stroke the dog.
Inés says: “He is very good. He likes it a lot!”
No, thanks. I look at the tower.
Inés says: “The clock is very old.”
The tower clock rings: it is twelve o’clock! Inés asks: “Are you hungry?” What do you say?
Where are you from?
I am from…
What is your city like?
Is there a big square?
Do you like dogs?
Yes, a lot. / I prefer cats.
Do you have a dog?
What is its name?
Do you take many photos?
Yes, many. / No, few.
With your phone?
Of what?
What time is it now?
It is…
What time do you eat?
What time do you go to sleep?
the square
the tower
the clock
the dog
the photo

Bariloche’s Centro Cívico has buildings made of stone and cypress wood, in a style similar to Alpine villages. From the square you can see the lake. Inés gives free guided tours every morning and tourists leave her a tip.
Many tourists think these buildings are old, from Switzerland. But they are from 1940 and an Argentine architect built them! Today I have a group of twelve people from six countries. Will you join?
The tour ends. Inés asks what you want to see next. What do you choose?
The Patagonia museum.
You see objects of the Mapuche and Tehuelche peoples. Inés explains there were no borders here before.
The cathedral, near the lake.
You walk ten minutes along the lakeside. The cathedral has very beautiful stained-glass windows.
A place to eat something typical.
Inés recommends a tea house with Welsh cake and raspberry jam.
A tourist from the group doesn’t tip and leaves quickly. Inés says nothing. What do you do?
Do you take guided tours when you travel?
Yes, always. / No, I prefer going alone.
Which was the best?
Do you leave a tip?
What is the most beautiful building in your city?
For me it is… because…
Is it old?
Can you visit it?
Do you like museums?
Yes, especially … ones. / Not much.
Which is your favourite?
Who do you go with?
Do people tip in your country?
Yes, usually ten per cent. / No, it is not common.
Where?
What do you think about tipping?
the guided tour
the tip
the building
the waterfront
to join

Inés is preparing a new tour about the history of Bariloche. While she looks for information in the city archive, she finds letters from an immigrant family who arrived in 1903. In one of them, a woman tells how she crossed the Andes from Chile in winter, with two children and a cow.

I read the letter three times. This woman walked for twenty days in the snow and then wrote: “We have arrived. The lake is so big it looks like the sea.” And nobody remembers her. The books only talk about the men who founded the city. Do you know how your family came to the place where they live?
How should Inés use these letters?
Read a letter aloud at the end of each tour.
Many tourists are moved. Some write to her afterwards to tell their own family’s story.
Look for the family’s descendants.
She finds a great-granddaughter who lives three blocks away. She knew nothing about the letters.
Suggest an exhibition to the museum.
The museum accepts, but says it will take a year. Inés starts writing the texts that same night.
In the last letter, the woman mentions “Mrs Inés, who helped us cross.” It is the same name as the guide, and she was her great-great-grandmother.
Do you know where your family came from?
My grandparents / great-grandparents came from…
Why did they leave?
Who told you?
Do you keep old letters or photos?
Yes, I have… from my… / No, everything is on my phone.
Which is the oldest?
Where do you keep them?
What difficult journey did someone in your family make?
My… travelled to… in…
How long did it take?
Why did they do it?
Who deserves to be in history books and isn’t?
I think… because…
Why do you think they aren’t?
What did they do?
the archive
the letter
the mountain range
the descendant
the great-granddaughter

In the Centro Cívico square there is a statue of a 19th-century military officer. For many he is a national hero; for the Mapuche communities, he is responsible for the violent occupation of their lands. One group wants it removed, another wants it protected. The town council asks Inés, as a guide, to propose the text for a new sign next to the statue.

Every day, in front of that statue, someone asks me who he was. If I say “a hero”, some get angry; if I say “a perpetrator of genocide”, others do. I believe a guide is not there to tell people what to think, but to give the full picture. But how do you sum up a hundred years of conflict in fifty words? What would you write?
